newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania Democrats sweep to victory in local poll.
newsitem.headline: Albania Democrats sweep to victory in local poll.

text.p: Albania's ruling Democratic Party won a clear majority of city halls, regional and communal councils in local elections at the weekend, the Central Electoral Commission said on Friday.

The Democrats seized 88 percent of city halls in Sunday's vote, up from 51 percent in 1992 elections. They also took 62.5 percent of communes, up from 37 percent and 52.5 percent of the vote for regional councils compared with 43 percent last time.

The key opposition Socialists won 9.5 percent of city halls, down from 35 percent, and 3.9 percent of communes, down from 45 percent. They gained 31 percent of the vote for regional councils, compared with 41 percent in 1992.
The official results decide the political make-up of 42 city halls, 212 communes and 36 regional councils.
A run-off on Sunday will decide the fate of another 22 city halls and 96 communes, the central commission said.
The Socialists, reformed heirs to the communists, have criticised the way the poll was conducted but most independent observers have concluded it was fair.
The local ballot came five months after a general election, which was boycotted by most opposition parties amid accusations of vote rigging.
